Irene / team — quick triage:
- Observed: surge of upstream 502/504s from regional edge proxies in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 between 07:38–08:10 UTC. Error rate peaked at ~22% for a 10m window.
- Signal correlation: simultaneous spike in client retry rate from BlueCove SDKs (excessive exponential retry leading to connection churn).
- Root suspects: (A) upstream backend autoscaling recently completed a rolling scale-out; health-check propagation lag left a small subset of warm nodes behind, (B) edge load balancer queue depth limit hit which caused connection resets when backend response latency increased, and (C) SDK retry amplification amplified the feedback loop.

Immediate mitigations executed (08:26–08:34 UTC):
1) Enabled stricter circuit breaker on edge for BlueCove routes (short-circuit to 503 fallback after 3 failed attempts).
2) Increased per-edge worker pool and bumped connection timeout from 10s -> 18s to allow in-flight responses to succeed while backends finish warm-up.
3) Initiated targeted scale-up of edge fleet in ap-southeast-1 by +120% (rolling capacity request to infra).
4) Outreach to BlueCove asking them to reduce client retry aggressiveness and enable jitter (see suggested retry policy below).

Early result: error rate dropped to ~6% by 08:33 UTC in APAC and to ~4% in EU. We are continuing to monitor.

Logs: small snippets captured and stored as edge_config_patch.diff and bluecove_error_samples.txt. Token-level tracing attached to incident.
